+## Local integration against a running platform-framework
+
+IAM holds **no platform-framework credential of its own**: every outbound PF
+call forwards the caller's own `Authorization` header, so the read runs with the
+caller's identity and permissions. platform-framework's `/v2` API accepts **HTTP
+Basic only**, so only a Basic caller is forwardable — a Bearer caller (Auth0, or
+a local `pnpm dev` / e2e ephemeral token) falls back to the permissive org-level
+check. So plain `pnpm dev`, which hands out Bearer tokens, never reaches a real
+platform-framework even though `PLATFORM_FRAMEWORK_ENABLED` defaults to on.
+
+E2E goes further and turns the flag off outright — `scripts/test-e2e-local.sh`
+starts the dev server with `PLATFORM_FRAMEWORK_ENABLED=false`, and CDK sets the
+same on the ephemeral Lambda — so the suite stays fully mocked whichever
+credential it presents. Running the two-terminal workflow by hand, pass
+`PLATFORM_FRAMEWORK_ENABLED=false` to `pnpm dev` yourself to match.
+
+To exercise IAM's **real** HTTP client (`getConfigVars`, `getSitesForAccount`,
+`getLegacyUserRoles`, `getSiteConfig`, account-level `rolesv2`) against a
+locally-running platform-framework:
+
+**1. Boot platform-framework and get a credential.** In your
+`platform-framework` checkout run `make provision` — it seeds account **1501 /
+site 1** and serves v2 at `http://localhost/v2/...` (plain HTTP is accepted
+locally). Create a **backoffice API user** (log in as `support@sitoo.com` / `no`,
+add an API user for account 1501); the credential is `1501-<apiuserid>` : `<pw>`.
+
+**2. Point IAM at it.** In `services/iam-api/.env`:
+
+```sh
+PLATFORM_FRAMEWORK_BASE_URL=http://localhost   # origin override (scheme + host[:port])
+```
+
+That is the only setting the client needs — the credential travels with each
+request, and `PLATFORM_FRAMEWORK_ENABLED` is already on by default. Leave
+`BASE_URL` empty to route by nodeId to the production `https` host.
+
+**3. Exercise via the dev server.** `pnpm dev` runs the real `rolesv2`
+middleware, and the account-level check forwards the caller's credential — so
+call the dev server with the **same PF Basic credential** rather than a local
+Bearer token. The dev server has no auth Lambda to validate Basic against, so
+tell it which identity to assume (local only — no deployed env sets these):
+
+```sh
+# services/iam-api/.env
+LOCAL_BASIC_AUTH_ORGANIZATION_ID=<org uuid>
+LOCAL_BASIC_AUTH_USER_ID=<user id>
+LOCAL_BASIC_AUTH_ACCOUNT_ID=1501
+LOCAL_BASIC_AUTH_NODE_ID=100
+```
+
+```sh
+curl -s http://localhost:3000/v1/roles \
+  -u '1501-<apiuserid>:<pw>'
+```
+
+Notes:
+- The `/v1/test/token` Bearer token still works for everything else, but it is
+  **not** forwardable to platform-framework — requests using it fall back to the
+  permissive org-level `rolesv2` check.
+- With `PLATFORM_FRAMEWORK_BASE_URL` set, `node_id` is ignored for routing (the
+  override origin wins); it still selects the mock-vs-real config-var value in
+  the response.
+- `userExistsInSite` still uses the mock (ticket 04), and its real URL is missing
+  a `.json` suffix — do not rely on it against real platform-framework yet.
+

+## Role terminology
+
+Canonical forms, to avoid drift between modules:
+
+- **`slug`** — a role's own identifier (`roles` table, `Role.slug`, `RoleSchema.slug`). Lowercase, hyphenated, `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`.
+- **`roleSlug`** (domain) / **`role_slug`** (wire, CDC) — the same slug value as seen from `role-assignments`. Two names for one concept because the assignment is a separate entity that references a role by slug — not an inconsistency to "fix", just note both exist.
+- **Legacy role slug** — one of `admin`, `staff`, `store-manager`, `store-staff` (`LEGACY_ROLE_SLUGS` / `LegacyRoleSlug` in `legacy-translation.ts`). Always hyphenated — matches platform-framework's own slug convention (`ApiSessionPermission`) and IAM's `RESERVED_SLUGS`. Do not reintroduce an underscored form; a prior inconsistency here caused `/role-by-slug/store-manager` to silently miss the legacy path.
+- **System role slug** — a `sitoo-*` slug from `system-roles.catalog.ts` (e.g. `sitoo-admin`, `sitoo-store-manager`). Each legacy role slug maps to one system role slug plus a client and a platform-framework role integer (10/20/30/40) via the single `LEGACY_MAPPINGS` table in `legacy-translation.ts` — never duplicate that mapping elsewhere.
+- **`is_system`** (DB column) / **`isSystemRole`** (domain) / **`is_system_role`** (wire) — one concept, three names by layer (DB snake_case without suffix, domain camelCase, wire snake_case). Layered convention, not a bug.
+
+`franchise-admin` does not exist — no catalog entry, no mapping. Legacy `admin` resolves to `admin` on every site, franchise or not.
+
 ## System roles
 
-Defined in `src/modules/roles/system-roles.catalog.ts`: admin, franchise-admin, staff, store-manager, store-staff.
+Defined in `src/modules/roles/system-roles.catalog.ts`: `sitoo-admin`, `sitoo-head-office-user`, `sitoo-store-manager`, `sitoo-store-staff`, `sitoo-viewer`.
 
 System roles are **materialized as real database rows** (`is_system = 1`) — not synthesized at query time. They cannot be modified or deleted via the API. Orgs can override individual permissions via the `role_permissions` table.
